messages:
amelia: Heads up — after last canary deploy I'm seeing PP-bubble variance on 1F1B runs for 64-token seqs. Tail latency spikes ~18% on 8-GPU jobs. nvprof/nsys traces attached in the run. Kernel selection looks noisy, maybe tuner thrash. Anyone else seeing this?

juan: Yep, reproduced on canary. Noticed autotuner flipping between fp16_fused and int8_path on a couple of transformer layers mid-epoch. When it flips, all-reduce overhead balloons.

kai: Quick trace excerpt from nsys (trimmed):
```
Timeline: model=redwood-3b, microbatch=4, 8 gpus
MatMul_forward: 420ms
AllReduce_grad: 320ms (blocked overlap windows)
Kernel_switch: 68ms (recompiles / kernel select jitter)
KV_cache_flush: 112ms (microbatch boundary flushes)
Other overhead: 80ms
```

sophie: Related note — KV cache hit rate drops ~6% with microbatch=4 because we flush partial prefixes between microbatches in current impl. That increases memcopies and changes seq-length distribution seen by tuner.

amelia: Hypothesis: small microbatch -> more frequent KV flushes + shorter compute chunks -> insufficient compute to hide all-reduce latency under 1F1B. Also autotuner sees transient seq patterns and switches kernels mid-run, adding overhead. Proposed experiments: (1) sweep microbatch={4,6,8,12}, (2) force kernel-lock after warmup, (3) set kv_cache_mode=sticky to avoid flushes.

juan: Ran a quick A/B: microbatch=4 vs 8 on same model + dataset (short convo workload). Profile summary (median over 10 iters):
```
mb=4: AllReduce=32% total time, MatMul=40%, KernelSwitch=8%, KVFlush=10%
mb=8: AllReduce=12% total time, MatMul=55%, KernelSwitch=3%, KVFlush=4%
```
So increasing microbatch reduces relative AllReduce walltime and KV flushes.

kai: Also spotted memcpy spikes (CPU->GPU) correlated with KV_flush events at mb=4. That explains the intermittent tail spikes. We should check host-side batching heuristics and pinned-memory reuse.

amelia: Good catch. Actionable items:
- Run microbatch sweep with kernel-lock enabled after 200 iters warmup
- Add seq-length aware kernel selection: prefer stable kernel if variance < 5% over last N steps
- Toggle kv_cache_mode sticky vs flush and measure cache-hit and memcpy counts
- Capture nsight snapshots around kernel_switch events

infra-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-17T17:10:20 completed for service=pp-runtime-canary, commit=ae3f8d. No infra alerts.

juan: I'll queue perf-sweep on perf-swarm (slots=6) and attach profiling artifacts. Script: `python infra/perf/run_pp_sweep.py --microbatches 4,6,8,12 --kv sticky,flush --kernel-lock true --warmup 200`

kai: I'll add a lightweight kernel-lock flag to runtime (prefer-stable-after-warmup). PR draft soon. Also suggest adding a small debounce in the autotuner to avoid flipping on single-batch anomalies.

sophie: I'll run KV cache hit analysis and push a dashboard panel for memcpy spikes vs kv-flush events.

amelia: Cool. If the sweep confirms, next step is a canary with mb=8 default for 8-GPU pools and enable kernel-lock for first 15 minutes. Keeping an eye on quality regressions. :eyes:  

juan: Added follow-up tasks to perf board. Will post results here when done. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
